entries.description: Left out when there are none.

facets.description: Left out when there are none.

DiagramResult_SearchEntry.description: `/search/diagram/{id}` and `/search/fireworks`: the entries, their type facets, Solr's count.

reviseDate.description: Like the TOC's, omitted when there is none. Measured over the 669 pathways `/data/content/doi` returns: `reviseDate` absent in 564, `releaseStatus` in 608, and the people lists in a few -- `authors` 3, `reviewers` 11, `editors` 12.

EpochMillis.description: A date written as milliseconds since the epoch.

targetResults.description: For a search that found nothing: the terms, and whether each is a target.

GroupedResult_SearchEntry.description: `/search/query`: the groups, the rows written, the groups and matches Solr counted.

Highlighted.description: Text Solr may have highlighted: a match is wrapped in `…`, so a reader showing it as plain text escapes it.

id.description: The stId, or the dbId when there is none; never highlighted.

icon.description: Java's getter: an icon has a name.

summation.description: The icon's description. Icons have no inferred one to fall back to.

items.description: One physical entity an icon draws; an empty part is left out.

IconEntry.description: An icon of the icon library.

IconResult.description: `/search/icon/query`: the icon library's page, one ungrouped group of icons.

Long.description: A Java long, written exactly (`JSON.rawJSON`): it may exceed 2^53, beyond which a JavaScript number reads it rounded.

PathwayOfEntry.description: What `/search/pathways/of/{dbId}` answers: pathways, written with only the fields the pathway browser asks for (`fields=DB_ID,ST_ID,NAME,HAS_EHLD`), so no type.

entries.description: Left out when the group has none (an ungrouped search that found none).

typeName.description: Left out for a group Solr names with nothing.

ResultGroup_IconEntry.description: One group of results: a type's, or "Results" for a search not grouped.

entries.description: Left out when the group has none (an ungrouped search that found none).

typeName.description: Left out for a group Solr names with nothing.

ResultGroup_SearchEntry.description: One group of results: a type's, or "Results" for a search not grouped.

children.description: Left out on a class with no subclasses (74 of the 106).

id.description: The stId, or the dbId when there is none; never highlighted.

hasReferenceEntity.description: Always false: an event has no reference entity.

oneOf.description: A pathway or a reaction. A reaction's `exactType` is its category (binding, transition, ...).

id.description: The stId, or the dbId when there is none; never highlighted.

anyOf.description: The physical-entity classes the indexer names a type by: those neither a set nor genome-encoded. Every reference-entity class has a type of its own. entity-types.spec.ts derives the list from the domain snapshot.

type.description: The indexer's types for a physical entity or a reference entity (`getType`, `getReferenceTypes`); any other class goes by its own name. The list of those names is checked against the domain snapshot.

species.description: "Entries without species" when it has none.

oneOf.description: A physical entity or a reference entity.

id.description: The stId, or the dbId when there is none; never highlighted.

oneOf.description: A person, by name. No stId: `id` is the dbId. The counts are text, as Solr stores them.

id.description: The stId, or the dbId when there is none; never highlighted.

oneOf.description: A molecule known only from interaction data; `dbId` and `stId` are its accession.

id.description: The stId, or the dbId when there is none; never highlighted.

oneOf.description: An object of an earlier release, deleted since; its type and exactType are those it had.

SimpleDatabaseObject.description: graph-core's SimpleDatabaseObject as the content service writes it (simpleObjectJson, in tools/content-node/schema-endpoints.ts, which /instance/{id}/referrers writes with too). An object of a class without a stable id -- an InstanceEdit, a Species -- has no `stId`, and non_empty leaves it out; an empty displayName is left out the same way, and a missing one is written as the text "null". schemaClass is the class the labels name on /schema/{class}/min, always there; on /instance/{id}/referrers it is the object's property, "null" when missing and left out when empty.

SimplePerson.description:
The five fields Java's SimplePerson carries -- three of which are not always there.

`spring.jackson.default-property-inclusion=non_empty` in the content service means a null or empty field is omitted from the JSON rather than sent as null, so an absent value arrives as `undefined` and never as `null`. Measured over all 9,503 person entries the three content endpoints return: `dbId`, `displayName` and `surname` are always present; `firstname` is missing on 619 of them and `orcidId` on 3,961, and neither is ever null.

The declaration used to say otherwise, and three separate call sites had already worked around it -- `p.firstname?.toLowerCase()` in the contributors, contents and DOI searches, where `?.` on a required `string` is dead syntax that quietly says the author knew better than the type.

TargetResult.description: A term the search found nothing for, and whether it names a resource; an empty term or resource is left out.

doi.description: Omitted rather than sent null when there is none. Measured over the 34 top-level pathways `/data/content/toc` returns: `doi` absent in 29, `reviseDate` in 30, `releaseStatus` in 19. Declaring them required let `pathway.doi !== null` read as true for a field that is not there.

authors.description: Present on all 34 today, but the service leaves out an empty list rather than sending [] -- /data/content/doi omits each of the people lists for a few pathways -- so a top-level pathway without reviewers, or without subpathways, would come without the field.

doi.description:
Never sent, as far as anything here can tell.

`/data/content/toc` returns `stId`, `displayName` and `speciesName` for a child and nothing else -- measured over 215 nested subpathways, none of which carried a `doi`. `toc.component.html:161` renders a DOI link behind `@if (sub.doi)`, so that markup cannot fire today.

Left optional rather than deleted because it is not clear which side is wrong: the endpoint's child projection may be missing a field it should send, or the link may be markup for a case that never existed. Deleting the field would settle that question by forgetting it.
